newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau tourism shrinks as gang wars scare tourists.
newsitem.headline: Macau tourism shrinks as gang wars scare tourists.

text.p: Portuguese-governed Macau on Tuesday announced a sharp drop in tourism coinciding with a wave of violence linked to triad gangster wars.
The number of guests at Macau hotels shrank 23.3 percent in June, compared with the same month in 1996, the Statistics and Census Department said.
Guest numbers fell by 5.6 percent in the first half of the year, and the number using five-star hotels dropped by 15.1 percent.
The average hotel occupancy rate was down three points to 57.4 percent during the first half of the year.

The government-run Macau Tourist Office blamed the drop in tourists on news coverage by Hong Kong media on the crime wave in the Portuguese-run enclave -- violent clashes between triad gangsters, arson attacks, drive-by shootings and knifings.
Police link the incidents to clashes between triad gangs over proceeds from illegal protection and loan-sharking rackets feeding off Macau's legal casino business.

Macau relies on casino tourism for half its income. Casino magnate Stanley Ho said last week he believed tourism would pick up again this month, predicting an end to the mayhem that has scared away tourists.
Macau is due to revert to China in 1999.
